title: Will O'Rourke Ruled Out of India Series, Targets Australia Test Comeback
excerpt: New Zealand's 25-year-old quick will miss the ODIs and Tests against India as a “precaution,” with the December tour of Australia now his comeback target.
body:
• New Zealand fast bowler Will O'Rourke has been ruled out of the entire home series against India — five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests — as he continues rehabilitation for left hamstring and calf injuries, New Zealand Cricket confirmed on Saturday.
  • The 25-year-old, who was in contention for the ODI and Test squads, is being held back as a “precaution,” with the four-Test tour of Australia in December now his primary comeback target — ideally via a Canterbury return in the Plunket Shield and the Perth Test on December 9.
  • O'Rourke has endured a brutal 18 months: a back stress fracture kept him out seven months, a hamstring tear on the final day of the Nottingham Test against England in June was followed by a calf strain in training in late August.
  • New Zealand's injury list is growing — Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes were also ruled out of the T20I squad on Saturday, replaced by Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner.

New Zealand's pace attack has taken a serious hit ahead of India's tour, with strike bowler Will O'Rourke ruled out of the entire home series as he continues his rehabilitation from hamstring and calf injuries.

New Zealand Cricket confirmed on Saturday that the 25-year-old right-arm quick, who had been in contention for the ODI and Test squads, will miss all of India's visit — five T20Is starting October 22, five ODIs and two Tests — as a “precaution.” The decision pushes his return to international cricket to the four-Test tour of Australia in December.

“Disappointing for Will”

Head coach Rob Walter said the call was taken jointly with O'Rourke and the medical staff to give him time to rebuild his bowling loads without risking another setback.

“It's obviously disappointing for Will to have to miss such a marquee tour at home against India. We all agreed it was best for him to take some more time to rehabilitate both injuries and safely build up his bowling loads.”

— Rob Walter, New Zealand head coach

“Our pace bowling resources will be critical over the next few months so we're taking a conservative approach to Will's return to ensure he's fully fit before he takes the field again,” Walter added. “Ideally he'll be able to return for Canterbury in the Plunket Shield in late November, and in a perfect world he'll be ready to go for the opening Test against Australia in Perth on December 9.”

An 18-month injury nightmare

O'Rourke's absence continues a cruel run. A back stress fracture sidelined him for around seven months before he returned on New Zealand's tour of Bangladesh in April 2026, playing all three ODIs and taking five wickets. He then featured in all three Tests of the 2–1 series win in England in June, claiming 10 wickets — but tore his hamstring on the final day of the third Test in Nottingham. A calf strain in a late-August training session set his recovery back again, and he has not played international cricket since.

It is a significant loss: O'Rourke has taken 49 wickets in 14 Tests at an average under 25 since his 2024 debut, and he has not played a home international since April 2025.

More injury blows

New Zealand's casualty list grew further on Saturday, with batsman Mark Chapman and seamer Zak Foulkes both ruled out of the T20I squad. They were replaced by Josh Clarkson and Blair Tickner. The double blow leaves the Black Caps reshuffling both their batting and pace options less than two weeks before the series opener.

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora's cricket fans, O'Rourke's absence removes one of the tour's most compelling subplots — the hostile quick who troubled England in June bowling at India's batters on home decks. His duel with India's top order will now have to wait for another summer; the consolation is that a depleted New Zealand attack makes India's chances of a statement series win that much stronger.

What's next

The immediate question is who fills the new-ball void against India — and whether O'Rourke's conservative rehab timeline holds through to Perth. New Zealand's medical staff are betting that patience now buys them a fully fit spearhead for the defining assignment of their summer: four Tests in Australia.
